1.4 The Statistics Wing, called National Statistics Office (NSO), coordinates the statistical activities in
the country and is responsible for evolving and laying, down statistical standards. India is subscriber to the
International Monetary Fund’s (IMF) Special Data Dissemination Standards (SDDS) and is currently
fulfilling the Standards. The Ministry maintains an ‘Advance Release Calendar’ for its data categories
covered under the SDDS, which is disseminated on the Ministry’s website as well as on the Dissemination
Standards Bulletin Board (DSBB) of the IMF. The Ministry releases the datasets covered under the Real
Sector of SDDS through press notes and its website simultaneously. India has strong system of official
statistics and is among the leading countries in the area of official statistics. The Ministry’s officials have been
associated with international agencies on the development of methodologies, particularly in the areas of
national accounts, informal sector statistics, large- scale sample surveys, conduct of censuses, service sector
statistics, non-observed economy, social sector statistics, sustainable development goals, environmental
1.2 The Ministry has two wings viz. the Statistics Wing and the Programme Implementation (PI) Wing.
There is one Autonomous Body known as the Indian Statistical Institute (ISI), which is an institute of national
importance by an Act of Parliament, viz. The Indian Statistical Institute Act (ISI Act) 1959. It is renowned
and premier institute in the field of Statistics in the country. Also, National Statistical Commission (NSC),
which was created through Resolution of Government of India with effect from 12th July 2006 with
mandate to evolve policies, priorities and standards in statistical matters. The organisation chart of the
Ministry is at Annexure IIA and IIB.
1.3 MoSPI, being the nodal Ministry of the Government of India for all statistical matters, attaches
considerable importance to coverage and quality aspects of statistics released in the country. The statistics
released by the Ministry are based on administrative sources, surveys and censuses conducted by the Central
and State Governments, etc. The surveys conducted by the Ministry are based on scientific sampling
methods. Data is collected through dedicated field staff who are regularly trained in the concepts and
definitions of the items and the scope of the survey. In line with the emphasis on the quality of statistics
released by the Ministry, the methodological issues of the statistical products of this Ministry are overseen by
various committees viz, Advisory Committee on National Accounts, Technical Advisory Committee on
Statistics of Price and Cost of Living (TAC on SPCL), Steering Committee for National Sample Surveys
(NSS) along with various Advisory Groups/Expert Groups constituted from time to time as per requirement,
etc. National Sample Surveys are conducted on digital platform using Computer Assisted Personal
Interviewing(CAPI) and the e-SIGMA system The Ministry compiles data-sets based on current data, after
applying standard statistical techniques and extensive scrutiny and supervision.
1.1 The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) came into existence as an
independent Ministry on 15th October 1999 after the merger of the Department of Statistics and the
Department of Programme Implementation. The Ministry is the nodal agency for planning integrated
development of the statistical system in the country and coordination of statistical activities among different
stakeholders in Government of India, State Governments, Union Territories as well as meeting requirements
of the International Agencies. The Allocation of Business to the Ministry of Statistics and Programme

1.8 International Comparison Programme (ICP) is the largest statistical initiative in the world under the
aegis of United Nations Statistics Division (UNSD). The World Bank is implementing this programme at
global level and Asian Development Bank (ADB) is the nodal implementing agency at Asia and the Pacific
Region. The main objectives of ICP are to produce Purchasing Power Parities (PPPs) and Price Level Indices
and to convert volume and per capita measures of GDP into common currencies using PPPs. The World Bank
released the report of ICP 2021 cycle in August, 2025, which included data for India. According to these
results, India ranks as the third-largest economy globally.
1.5 The NSO, MoSPI is responsible for preparation of national accounts, which include the estimates of
Gross Domestic Product (GDP), National Income, Government/Private Final Consumption Expenditure,
Capital Formation and Saving along with details of transactions of institutional sectors. The Ministry
annually brings out publication titled “National Accounts Statistics”, containing these statistics. The
Ministry releases annual and quarterly estimates of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) from time to time as per
pre-specified schedule given in Advance Release Calendar. As per the First Advance Estimates of GDP for FY
2025-26 released on 7th January, 2026, the growth in real Gross Domestic Product (GDP) during 2025-26 is
estimated at 7.4 per cent as compared to the growth rate of 6.5 per cent in 2024-25. Real Gross Value Added
(GVA) at Basic Prices is estimated at 184.50 lakh crore in 2025-26, as against 171.87 lakh crore in 2024-
25, showing the growth of 7.3 per cent.
1.6 The Consumer Price Index (CPI) is designed to measure the changes over time in general level of
retail prices of selected goods and services that household purchase for the purpose of consumption. CPI
numbers are widely used as macroeconomic indicator of inflation. It is also used as tool by government and
Reserve Bank of India (RBI) for targeting inflation and monitoring price stability. CPI’s use as deflator in
the National Accounts also reflects its importance in measurement of economic health of the country. The
NSO, MoSPI releases data on Inflation and CPI on 12th of every month (or next working day, in case of 12th
being holiday). Therefore, time lag in release of this data is only 12 days which makes it one of the fastest
CPI across the world.
1.7 MoSPI released Consumer Price Index (CPI) on Base 2012=100 for All India Rural, Urban and
Combined for the month of December, 2025 (Provisional) which were 199.9, 195.9 and 198.0, showing an
annual inflation rate of 0.76%, 2.03% and 1.33% respectively. All-India Consumer Food Price Index (CFPI)
for the month of December, 2025 (Provisional) for Rural, Urban and Combined were 198.4, 205.9 and 201.1
respectively. All India year-on-year inflation rates for CFPI for the month of December, 2025 (Provisional)
for Rural, Urban and Combined sector were -3.08%, -2.09% and -2.71% respectively. The release contains
State-wise comprehensive inflation figures for the usage of various stakeholders.
1.9 The Price Statistics Division (PSD) of National Statistics Office, MoSPI is the nodal division for
implementing ICP in India and for providing data to ADB for inter-country validations and compilation of
PPP etc. The 2024 cycle of ICP has been started and MoSPI has also initiated price data collection and
collation work for this. The data for ICP is collected from different sources including Field Operations
Division (FOD) of MoSPI, Administrative Data, Surveys and Other Sources available with various
ministries. At present, ICP 2024 round is in progress.

1.10 The Index of Industrial Production (IIP) with base year 2011-12 is compiled and published by the
Economic Statistics Division (ESD) of MoSPI. The release timeline of IIP has been improved by reducing it
from six weeks to four weeks, ensuring timelier availability of industrial output data. It is published on the
28th of every month (or the next working day if 28th is holiday) with time lag of four weeks from the
reference month. The IIP covers three sectors namely Mining, Manufacturing and Electricity. The IIP for
2024-25 stands at 152.6, registering growth of 4%. The base year revision exercise of IIP is in progress and
Technical Advisory Committee (TAC) for the base year revision of IIP has been constituted on 27th
September 2024 for the same.
1.11 The Ministry is entrusted with the development of indicator framework for Sustainable Development
Goals (SDGs) in India to facilitate monitoring of SDGs. The Social Statistics Division of NSO developed
National Indicator Framework (NIF) for SDGs with identified data sources and periodicity for facilitating the
monitoring of the SDGs at national level. The framework is dynamic in nature and is reviewed and refined
every year. Presently, in SDG NIF 2025, there are 284 national indicators with identified data sources and
periodicity.The division also compiles Environment Account using United Nations System of Environmental
Economic Accounting Framework (UN SEEA Framework). The publications brought out by the Division
2025, Data Snapshot on Sustainable Development Goals National Indicator Framework Progress Report
2025, Sustainable Development Goals National Indicator Framework 2025, EnviStats India 2025:
Environment Statistics, “Environmental Accounting on forest -2025”, Women and Men in India, 2024:
Selected Indicators and Data and Ad hoc Publication Children in India 2025.
1.12 The National Sample Survey (NSS) under MoSPI is responsible for conducting large scale sample
surveys in diverse fields on all India basis. Primary data is collected regularly through nation-wide
household/enterprise surveys on various socio-economic subjects. Besides these surveys, the Ministry
collects data on rural and urban prices and also plays significant role in the improvement of crop statistics
through supervision of the area enumeration and crop estimation surveys of the State agencies. It also
maintains frame of urban area units for drawing samples in urban areas.
1.13 The MoSPI website (https://www.mospi.gov.in serves as an integrated digital platform for
statistical publications, reports, and visualization dashboards. It aims to provide seamless access to vital data
resources for stakeholders.
1.14 The Ministry has revamped and upgraded website for better dissemination of data to the users during
the year.
In order to address the need for providing greater insights from data to various stakeholders,
pool of more than 1700 data visualizations pertaining to key products of the Ministry e.g.
National Accounts Statistics, Consumer Price Index, Index of Industrial Production and NSS
surveys have been created and made available to users through its website.
separate category on User Suggested Visualizations has also been incorporated in the DataViz
section in an attempt to strengthen the statistical system through an institutionalized feedback
mechanism. These visualizations can be downloaded along with data adding value to the
datasets of the ministry by way of facilitating its reuse.
